Documentation

30 September, 2026

Today, I began testing out how I want to photograph the empty boxes. I made a makeshift photo studio on the floor of the family room, the room which houses many boxes. Funnily enough, when I asked my mom why she wasn't curious about what I was doing, she said that I do this kind of weird thing all the time.

I then pitched the idea of documenting all of the empty boxes my dad has accumulated to my mom. She said okay and laughed. She also made sure to clarify that she was not responsible for any of the boxes in the house.

4 October, 2026

Jane Bennett:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q607Ni23QjA&time_continue=902&source_ve_path=NzY3NTg&embeds_referring_euri=https%3A%2F%2Fcultivatingalternatives.com%2F

Foreground the non-human things and leave the humans who collect those things in the background. To see hoarders not as people with mental illness but as people who have special access to the calls of things

!Screenshot 2026-10-04 at 12.53.38 AM.png

the hoarder sees the shape, colour, texture, and form in great detail

Vibrant Matter: The Political Ecology of Things

“Sullivan reminds us that a vital materiality can never really be thrown "away," for it continues its activities even as a discarded or unwanted commodity. For Sullivan that day, as for me on that June morning, thing power rose from a pile of trash.” chapter 1 p6

Much like Sullivan and Bennett, the stacks and stacks of empty and repurposed cardboard boxes slowly taking over the house I’ve lived in for my whole life suddenly called to me as I began to pay more attention to things as things rather than mere objects

When I stop to look at the overwhelming amount of boxes, I am overcome with a harrowing sense emptiness. I feel the failed attempts at filling the void through mindless consumerism, only for the things these boxes formerly housed to be forgotten because the person who bought them held no affection for it in the first place. I spent a good portion of my childhood terrified of stepping foot into the basement. It was dark, cold, and simply an unnavigable maze of abandoned things, ever growing and only contained by my mother organizing and stacking boxes to make pathways for us to walk through. Each time a pathway got blocked, she would create a new, slimmer path.

10 October, 2026

In my ill and sleep deprived state, I ventured into my basement again after conducting some preliminary research on 9 boxes found in the family room. These are my findings amongst the towering piles of filled boxes, but I'm sure I will find more if I dig.

  • 7 golf club boxes
  • 5 large boxes that probably used to constrain large paintings or photographs
  • 2 empty Zara boxes
  • 1 prefolded box
  • Empty wine box
  • Nespresso machine box
  • Car floor mat box?
  • Unknown amount of folded up boxes near the stairs (currently inaccessible due to lack of light and preparation on my end to traverse so deep into the basement)

In the family room, I found:

  • one golf club box
  • 5 shoe boxes
  • One empty printer box

My findings tell me that the boxes are quickly outgrowing my humble studio setup in my room consisting of two black poster boards from dollarama and a stack of old notebooks as a tripod. I think I should start meeting the boxes where they are and transform my studio setup into a more mobile one, especially as the boxes get larger and more dirty (which I wouldn't want to bring into my room). However, this also means I may get questioned by my parents—I mean the Collector and his wife—more often as I begin to expand my operations throughout the whole house.

10 October, 2026

Today, the collector—unaware of my ongoing archival of his collection—mentioned that he wanted to clean up the shoe boxes and the gold club box in the family room within the next week, but he just “hadn’t had time to get to it” (translated from Cantonese to English as accurately as possible). Notably, he didn't not mention cleaning up the pile of boxes next to the couch, nor the large printer box that has been sitting there for around two years now, nor the large mess on the table in that same room, nor the hoard of boxes in the basement. I told him that I needed those boxes for my project and asked if I needed the “long box” (the golf club box) too because there were “plenty of those boxes downstairs.” This indicates he is aware of the identical empty boxes in the basement but does not do anything about them. He also pointed out where to find more shoeboxes: underneath the family room chairs for instance, showing once again, that he is aware of these boxes but does not do anything about them.
